entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: Eisenhower's Federal-Aid Highway Act (1956) built 77,000 km of controlled-access highways. Officially motivated by defense, the Interstates reshaped American geography — creating suburbs, strip malls, and the commuter lifestyle.
